The Coley Creek reservoir would straddle the State line, with one dam and part of the lake in Oconee County, South Carolina, and the other dam and the rest of the reservoir in Transylvania County, North Carolina. The powerhouse would be in Oconee County. Tax revenues generated by this project, therefore, would be divided between the two counties and States.
8.4 DESIGN ALTERNATIVES OF THE SELECTED PUMPED STORAGE
8.4.1 Powerhouse
The present trend in design of pump-turbines is to increase the machine speed in order to minimize costs. This means high specific speed, which requires deep setting of the pump-turbine unit to avoid unacceptable cavitation. Underground powerhouses can be built deep without unduly increasing costs, while setting a surface powerhouse as deep would result in more excavation and a more expensive structure. Also, the underground powerhouse would not have a significant visual impact on the environment and would offer a year-round construction program even under the most inclement weather.
8.4.2 Intake Structure in the Upper Reservoir
The morning-glory type intake structure would simplify the design of the trashrake structure; many technical difficulties have been experienced with trashrakes at some existing pumped storage plants. A horizontal type intake,* besides having a more complicated trashrake structure, would introduce additional hydraulic losses.
The Applicant's original plan was to locate the transformers in an underground vault contiguous to the powerhouse cavern. Additional studies have led the Applicant to redesign the project to locate the transformers above ground near the switchyard. The change of transformer location was based on consideration of economy, safety, reliability, and ease of operation and maintenance.
8.5 ENVIRONMENTAL AND ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT OF ALTERNATIVES
The FPC Staff has summarized the available data on the engineering aspects and environmental impacts of the proposed Bad Creek site, alternative sources of power, and alternative pumped storage sites. This summary is given in Table 8-7. As used here, "Denial of Application" refers to not building a pumped storage project, and to providing the power needs by an alternative method. Thus, there would be no impact relative to the proposed or alternative sites, although there would be those impacts associated with the alternative source utilized to provide the needed power.
